title: Clause complexity and accuracy
source: Language Learning Hub · original V4.4 teaching draft, not an external textbook
goal: Apply clause complexity and accuracy in an original academic-English context and explain reasoning in coherent English
context: 合并简单句时选择准确从句关系，不以句子长短判断水平。
grammar: relative clause 修饰名词，adverbial clause 说明时间、原因或让步。restrictive 从句限定对象，non-restrictive 补充信息通常用逗号；标点可能改变所指范围。
common_mistake: The students, who arrived early, got seats 暗示所指学生都早到；不能任意加逗号。

examples.text: Students who arrived early found seats near the front.
examples.note: 原文例句：结合本课知识讲解，辨认表达的功能与适用条件。

examples.text: This restrictive clause identifies a subset of the students.

reading: Students who arrived early found seats near the front. This restrictive clause identifies a subset of the students. If the clause were set off by commas, the sentence would present early arrival as additional information about the students already identified. A longer sentence is therefore not automatically a more accurate one. Writers need to decide which relationship they intend before combining ideas. Although complex structures can express useful distinctions, a clear short sentence remains preferable to a confusing chain of clauses.

questions.prompt: Does the first sentence state that every student arrived early ?
questions.answer: No, it identifies those who did.
questions.explanation: 限制性关系从句限定子集。

questions.prompt: Combine Some students needed help. They attended the workshop. without claiming all students needed help.
questions.answer: The students who needed help attended the workshop.
questions.explanation: 限制性从句明确群体；也可用 Some students needed help, so they attended…。

pronunciation: sentence stress; connected speech; intelligibility without a total score。先按意群朗读，再用选词面板练习；浏览器转写不能证明音素正确。
